message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI
on:
  - push
  - pull_request
jobs:
  test:
    name: Julia ${{ matrix.version }} - ${{ matrix.os }} - ${{ matrix.arch }} - ${{ github.event_name }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        version:
          - '1'
          - 'nightly'
        os:
          - ubuntu-latest
          - macOS-latest
        arch:
          - x64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - uses: julia-actions/setup-julia@v1
        with:
          version: ${{ matrix.version }}
          arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        env:
          cache-name: cache-artifacts
        with:
          path: ~/.julia/artifacts
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-test-${{ env.cache-name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Project.toml', '**/Manifest.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-test-${{ env.cache-name }}-
            ${{ runner.os }}-test-
            ${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: julia-actions/julia-buildpkg@v1
      - uses: julia-actions/julia-runtest@v1
      - uses: julia-actions/julia-processcoverage@v1
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v1
        with:
          file: lcov.info
",
  "rationale": "The workflow already caches Julia artifacts, but the cache key only hashes Project.toml. In Julia, Manifest.toml is the lockfile that pins exact dependency versions. Including it in the cache key ensures proper invalidation when dependencies change, improving cache hit rates and avoiding stale artifacts. This aligns with the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern's precondition that cache inputs should include the lockfile and environment. The change is minimal, preserves all test coverage, and does not introduce new permissions or network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200"]
}
